An event `2 a b` asks whether `a` and `b` are in the same group right now.

**Output.** For every event of type `2`, in order, print `YES` or `NO` on its own line.

Represent each group as a tree and let its root be the label. Two people are together exactly when their roots match.

editorial: Union-find keeps every group as a rooted tree stored in a `parent` array. `find(x)` walks to the root and then re-points every node on the way directly at the root (path compression). `union(a, b)` finds both roots and, if they differ, hangs the smaller tree under the larger (union by size). With both tricks the amortized cost per operation is `O(alpha(n))`, effectively constant.
